Subject: Instrumentation + contract sequencing for Marketplace listing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re gearing up to go-live on AWS Marketplace (SaaS) in Q3 and need to align on three things so procurement and billing flow cleanly:

1) Entitlement mapping: DataFoundry has 3 SKUs (Starter, Scale, Enterprise). Can you confirm the entitlement IDs you’ll register and whether entitlements support seat-based vs. usage-based proxies?

2) Webhook & metering schema: Our engineering team needs the webhook payload and signature algorithm for fulfillment events so we can reconcile invoices to our ledger.

3) Contract sequencing & proration: The procurement team expects the Redwood SaaS contract to be signed first, with AWS fulfillment attached as a downstream action. We need to confirm how proration is handled for mid-cycle license activations (monthly and annual).

We’ve attached the SaaS contract redacted and a short list of SKU mappings we expect. Can we schedule a 30-min hop tomorrow to lock owners? Ideally include someone who owns the webhook implementation and someone from sales ops for DocuSign flow.

Thanks,

Sarah Torres
Head of Partnerships, DataFoundry

Hi Sarah — great to get this started. High-level plan and owners below:

Plan
- Entitlement registration: Redwood will register entitlements for each SKU and provide entitlement IDs. We support both seat-proxy (for Starter/Scale) and a usage-proxy for the Enterprise tier if you opt to report usage.
- Webhook & metering: Ben will share a minimal webhook spec and a test endpoint. We recommend a canonical event with fields: product_sku, entitlement_id, timestamp, quantity, signature.
- Contract sequencing: Agree that Redwood SaaS contract should be countersigned first. AWS fulfillment (Marketplace listing + entitlement registration) follows. For proration: Redwood supports proration at the billing-account level; for Marketplace true-up we can coordinate invoice-level adjustments.

Next steps
- I attached an "instrumentation_checklist_v1.csv" with concrete items engineers can tick off.
- Ben, Monica: can one of you confirm the webhook HMAC header name and whether we should publish a test event URL?
- Sarah: please confirm the HubSpot deal ID (or we’ll create DF-2026-1187).

I’ll book 30 minutes for tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT if that works for your team.

Sarah / team — looping in a short technical stub:

Webhook basics (recommendation)
- Endpoint: POST https://hooks.datafoundry.io/redwood-metering/test
- Payload (JSON): {
  "product_sku": "string",
  "entitlement_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "quantity": number,
  "usage_unit": "tokens|requests|seats"
}
- Signature: header X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 of body, key exchanged out-of-band)
- Retry policy: 3 attempts with exponential backoff, 5xx = retry, 4xx = no retry

Attachment: I’ve attached a lightweight stub with example payloads for your engineers to run locally.

For proration: Redwood enforces proration on our billing account. On the Marketplace side we’ll coordinate the fulfillment type (SaaS contract + AWS entitlements) so that AWS invoices reflect the usage/seat counts we report. If DataFoundry wants platform-level billing consolidation, we should schedule a meeting with AWS Metering to confirm the billing path.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Manager, Integrations | Redwood Inference

Hello DataFoundry & Redwood team,

Thanks for the details. Quick confirmations from AWS Metering:

- Entitlement registration: We can register the entitlements once the SaaS Contract is countersigned and when you provide the finalized SKU-entitlement mapping. Please submit the mapping spreadsheet to the Seller Central metering team.
- Fulfillment type: For your described flow we recommend the "SaaS Contract" fulfillment (with entitlement mapping) rather than the License + Metering hybrid — it avoids double-billing.
- Proration and invoices: AWS invoices for Marketplace charges are issued monthly on the AWS account owner. Proration for mid-cycle activations is not automatically handled by AWS in all cases; recommended approach is: (a) Redwood reports usage/seat counts as events, (b) DataFoundry issues customer-facing credits or adjustments through your own billing system, and (c) AWS invoices reflect aggregated charges. We can provide a sample reconciliation report.

Action items for next week:
- DataFoundry: upload finalized SKU mapping and SaaS contract (redacted ok) to Seller Central and share link with us.
- Redwood: provide entitlement_id list and a staging webhook test endpoint.
- We will schedule a short sync with Seller Central metering ops to confirm timeline for registration (typical SLA 3–5 business days after submission).

Reference attachments: FulfillmentGuide_AWS.pdf (high-level), see also AWS documentation for SaaS fulfillment.

Regards,
